implementation.standaloneHTML: Render Markdown as h1-h4/p/hr/strong/em/text nodes using document.createElement and document.createTextNode
implementation.reactCandidate: Import the identical parseResearchMarkdown function from research-markdown.mjs and create React elements without dangerouslySetInnerHTML
implementation.parserParity: Node test checks parser source embedded in standalone HTML is byte-identical to exported parser implementation apart from module export
implementation.allowedMarkup: Paragraphs, headings # to ####, bold **...**, italic *...*, horizontal rule ---
implementation.unsupportedMarkup: Tables, lists, nested inline markup, arbitrary links, full CommonMark and raw HTML
implementation.injectionDefense: HTML-looking strings remain literal text nodes, not parsed HTML; no innerHTML

readerUsability.before: Raw Markdown symbols ### and ** displayed in historical prose
readerUsability.after: Semantic heading/strong/emphasis/rule displayed with readable paragraphs
readerUsability.beforeAfterMobileScreenshot: Created in local conversation artifact, not pushed to GitHub

limitations: A safe minimal Markdown grammar is not a full Markdown renderer; unsupported syntax must remain literal instead of inventing markup.
Standalone HTML has an embedded parser for offline use; the React candidate imports the matching module; parity is tested by exact source extraction.
Browser QA used page.set_content of the complete source; production app and network deployment were not tested.
No WebKit, actual screen-reader human assessment, historical expert approval, real-reader pilot or authenticated AI Studio host deployment has been performed.
The research branch is public; canShip=false is a release flag and does not restrict access to published GitHub file bytes.
nextRecommendedWork: Focus on a real-reader walkthrough of L0/L1 distinction and historical evidence comprehension before expanding to more events. Keep research gate false until historians and production host are verified.
